issues.legal_issue: A delegated land-classification schedule is valid when its classifications are based on the statutory criteria of yield and soil quality and the record does not show that it departs from those criteria.
material_facts: The landowners challenged the classification schedule used to convert land into standard acres, arguing that it did not assess yield and soil quality as required.
The schedule divided land into classes by district and assessment circle, taking account of factors including soil, irrigation, location, fertility, and produce.
The landowners produced no affidavit or document showing that the schedule departed from the statutory criteria.
issues.conclusion: The classification schedule complied with the statutory criteria and was constitutionally valid; the challenge to its validity failed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(5) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953 requires classification according to quantity of yield and quality of soil. Section 27 authorizes rules to carry out the Act's purposes. The Court relied on Jagir Singh v. State of Punjab, which upheld a classification schedule based on relevant settlement and assessment factors.

rule.if: land_tenure_surplus_area_appeal and classification_schedule_challenged and schedule_based_on_yield_and_soil_factors and no_evidence_of_departure

predicates.land_tenure_surplus_area_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in a land-tenure dispute about the determination of surplus area.
predicates.classification_schedule_challenged: A party challenges a delegated schedule used to classify land for conversion into standard units.
predicates.schedule_based_on_yield_and_soil_factors: The schedule classifies land using factors relating to its yield and soil quality.
predicates.no_evidence_of_departure: The challenging party provides no evidence that the schedule departs from the governing classification criteria.

issues.definition: When a surplus-area appeal challenges a classification schedule, the schedule is valid if it is based on yield and soil factors and no evidence shows a departure from those factors.

issues.legal_issue: Land omitted as a distinct class from the applicable district schedule may be valued as unirrigated land when the district had no such class of land when the schedule was made.
material_facts: The landowners' land was recorded as sailab or adna sailab land in the revenue records.
The schedule for the relevant district listed other land classes but did not list sailab or adna sailab land.
The record showed no sailab land in that district when the rules and classification were made.
The revenue authorities treated the land as unirrigated land; valuing it by reference to the sailab classification for another district would have produced a higher valuation.
issues.conclusion: The revenue authorities correctly treated the land as unirrigated land, and the challenge to that classification failed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Annexure A to the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Rules, 1953, interpreting the district-specific schedule in light of its listed land classes and the circumstances existing when the classification was made. It held that the land could not be left without valuation merely because its recorded description was absent from the district schedule.

predicates.land_tenure_surplus_area_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in a land-tenure dispute about the determination of surplus area.
predicates.land_type_absent_from_district_schedule: The applicable district schedule does not list the land's recorded type as a distinct class.
predicates.district_lacked_land_type_when_classifie: The district had no land of that type when the classification schedule was made.

issues.definition: In a surplus-area appeal, land of a type absent from the district schedule may be assigned the unirrigated classification when the district lacked that type of land at the time of classification.

issues.legal_issue: Land does not qualify for a special valuation under specified proviso categories when its type is outside the land classes those provisos cover.
material_facts: The landowners argued that the land should receive the benefit of the special valuation provisions for specified categories of land.
Their land was described as sailab or adna sailab land.
The specified proviso categories addressed banjar qadim, banjar jadid, and cultivated thur land subject to waterlogging, and did not cover sailab or adna sailab land.
issues.conclusion: The landowners were not entitled to the benefit of any of those proviso categories.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 2, provisos (a), (b), and (c), of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Rules, 1953 provides special valuation treatment for the categories it specifies. The Court held that those provisions do not extend to land of a different type not included in their terms.

predicates.land_tenure_surplus_area_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in a land-tenure dispute about the determination of surplus area.
predicates.land_type_outside_special_valuation_cate: The land's type is not among the types covered by the special valuation categories.

issues.definition: In a surplus-area appeal, land outside the specified special valuation categories does not receive the benefit of those categories.
